samples.summary: Escaping switched from SQL-standard quote doubling to mysql2 backslash escapes, which breaks (or is bypassable) if StarRocks runs with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES/ANSI sql_mode
samples.evidence: `sql()` now returns `mysql.escape(value)`, which emits `\'` and `\\` rather than the previous `''` doubling. The previous form is valid in both MySQL default mode and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES/ANSI_QUOTES modes; the new form only in the default mode. If a StarRocks deployment (or a connection default) disables backslash escapes, a document id containing a quote produces a syntactically broken/injectable literal — and the failure would be silently swallowed by the try/catch in getWorkspaceAnalytics (returns enabled+zeros), so the dashboard shows wrong numbers rather than an error. Nothing in the change pins the session sql_mode.

samples.summary: `r.canManage &&` silently hides the Details link when the field is absent (version skew / any other producer), with no fallback
samples.evidence: The link now renders only when `r.canManage` is truthy. The field is brand new on the API response; during a rollout where the frontend is newer than the backend (or a cached response), every row's `canManage` is `undefined`, so even a workspace owner loses all Details links with no indication why. There is no defaulting (e.g. `r.canManage !== false`) and no runtime shape check in getWorkspaceAnalytics (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:264), which just returns res.json().

samples.summary: Workspace analytics page still shows the generic failure text on a 403, while the sibling detail page was given a specific message
samples.evidence:
document-analytics.tsx now branches on `error instanceof HttpError && error.status === 403`, but workspace-analytics.tsx line 39 keeps `if (error) return
Failed to load analytics.
;`. The workspace endpoint throws ForbiddenException for non-members (analytics.controller.ts:222 via WorkspaceService.assertMember), so a non-member landing on a shared workspace-analytics URL gets an unexplained generic failure — the exact case the change set out to fix, left unhandled on the member-gated page.

samples.summary: `mysql.escape` is imported from the promise wrapper; if `mysql2/promise` does not re-export `escape`, every warehouse query throws a TypeError
samples.evidence: `sql()` calls `mysql.escape` where `mysql` is `import * as mysql from 'mysql2/promise'`. mysql2's promise entrypoint re-exports the core helpers in current versions, but if it does not (or in the pinned ^3.23.0 typings), `mysql.escape` is undefined and every buildQueries/buildWorkspaceQueries call throws before any query runs — the document dashboard would 500 (getDocumentAnalytics builds queries outside its try block, line 119). mysql2 is not installed in this checkout so I could not verify the export.
